title: Tiered fallback marginal cost playbook — WIP
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working playbook for computing marginal cost for multi-tier fallback policies (Tier0 = pinned dedicated, Tier1 = regional spot, Tier2 = on-demand cross-region) and turning those numbers into simple, production-safe routing rules. Goal: give Product+Optimize a short, actionable heuristic that SRE/Serving can run in the console as a rule set or we can bake into the smart-router.

High-level idea (one sentence): choose the lowest-cost tier that satisfies a per-request latency SLO with a safety multiplier for spot revocations and cross-region network overhead.

Open questions (high priority):
- How to fold revocation probability into per-token marginal cost (expected additional cost of fallback + tail latency impact)?
- Should we expose an explicit margin parameter per-customer (conservative vs aggressive)?
- How to represent costs for mixed-model workflows (e.g., embeddings + chat in same request path)?

Quick glossary (for this doc):
- Base-cost: direct per-token cost on a tier (compute + infra unit).
- Revocation penalty: expected extra tokens/requests routed to fallback when spot loses capacity (including queueing, rerun, and overhead).
- Latency premium: measured additional p95 (ms) when routing to fallback (network hops, cold start).
- Safety factor: scalar >1 to inflate base-cost when revocation risk or SLAs require conservatism.

Assumptions used in the worked examples below (feel free to update after experiments):
- Spot revocation rate (regional) = 0.6% per hour under current markets (observed Aug–Sep 2025).
- Average request token length = 60 tokens.
- Base per-token cost on tiers: Tier0 (dedicated) = $0.0009/token; Tier1 (spot regional) = $0.00035/token; Tier2 (on-demand cross-region) = $0.0016/token.
- Cross-region network add-on cost (bandwidth + egress) = $0.00002/token.
- Cold-start rerun penalty (when spot revokes mid-request) = additional 6 tokens on average due to retry/late-arrival of KV cache.

Marginal expected cost calculation (per-request, simplified):
- E(cost_tier) = base_cost_per_token * expected_tokens + revocation_rate * fallback_penalty_cost + cross_region_addon
- fallback_penalty_cost = (tokens_lost_due_revocation * fallback_base_cost) + (latency_sla_violation_cost if measured)

Worked example (concrete numbers):
- Request tokens = 60
- Tier1 base cost = 60 * $0.00035 = $0.021
- Revocation expected rerun cost = 0.006 revocations/hour means per-request revocation_probability P_r ≈ 0.006 * (request_duration_hours). With average inference duration ~0.5s (0.0001389 hours), P_r ≈ 8.3e-7 ≈ negligible for short requests. BUT for longer streaming sessions (e.g., 30s), P_r ≈ 0.000208 (~0.02%).
- For conservative estimate assume P_r = 0.0002 for mid-length sessions: rerun tokens = 6 tokens * fallback base (Tier2) $0.0016 = $0.0096; expected rerun cost = 0.0002 * $0.0096 ≈ $0.00000192
- Cross-region addon (if fallback is cross-region) = 60 * $0.00002 = $0.0012
- E(cost_Tier1) ≈ $0.021 + $0.000002 + $0.0012 ≈ $0.0222
- Compare to Tier2 (on-demand): 60 * $0.0016 + 60*$0.00002 = $0.096 + $0.0012 = $0.0972
- Tier0 (dedicated): 60 * $0.0009 = $0.054

Interpretation: raw numbers show Tier1 (spot) is ~2.5x cheaper than Tier0 for these short requests. But two non-cost factors push us toward Tier0 for latency-sensitive SLOs: (1) variance in p95 due to revocations and warmup, (2) operational complexity when a customer cannot tolerate the tiny but non-zero fallback probability.

Heuristic routing rules (initial draft):
1) SLO-driven default rule:
   - If customer_p95_target <= 150ms -> prefer Tier0 (dedicated) unless expected marginal cost of Tier1 is < 0.5 * Tier0 AND historical revocation incidents per-week on chosen region < 3.
2) Cost-first rule (PLG customers):
   - If customer_p95_target > 300ms -> prefer Tier1 spot by default. Apply safety factor 1.15 to Tier1 marginal cost to account for seasonality.
3) Mixed strategy for streaming/long sessions (>5s):
   - Use Tier0 for request start and attach Tier1 for subsequent low-priority tokens (prefix caching + local KV) OR prefer Tier0 if session length > 20s.
4) Canary/fallback thresholds:
   - Define low-capacity threshold X% (e.g., 70%) for a pool; when available capacity < X, proactively shift new sessions to Tier0 to avoid mid-session revocations.

Operational knobs to expose in Console (minimum viable set):
- safety_factor (float), per-customer override
- max_session_duration_for_spot (seconds)
- region_blacklist/whitelist (for spot preference)
- fallback_order (list: e.g., [dedicated, spot-regional, on-demand-crossregion])

Experiment plan to validate numbers (2–4 week cadence):
- A/B test: 2% traffic on Tier1 vs Tier0 for customers with p95 targets 200–300ms. Measure: true p95, revocation incidents, cost per request, customer-visible error/retry rate. (JIRA-OPT-581)
- Synthetic revocation injection: artificially withdraw X% of spot nodes for a short window to measure real rerun token counts and latency tails (include SRE runbook).
- Historical backtest: run last 30 days of traffic through simulator using real token length distributions and observed spot revocation timestamps (github.com/redwood-inference/routing-sim).

Notes on modelling pitfalls and conservative adjustments:
- Don’t ignore correlated failures: spot pools in a region see correlated churn during maintenance/market spikes. Use a region-level correlation multiplier (conservative default 2x revocation probability) when a customer SLAs require low risk.
- Network egress can dominate for very long token windows (>500 tokens); include bandwidth regression into marginal cost for those tails.
- Quantization/latency tradeoffs: cheaper quantized model variants on spot might increase per-token latency — treat them like distinct tiers in the model.

Deliverables for next two weeks:
- Simulator run and CSV export with per-customer marginal cost deltas (Priya) — target: 2025-11-09
- JIRA-OPT-581: A/B experiment spec (Miguel) — target: 2025-11-05
- Draft Console UI control spec listing knobs + default presets (Ava) — target: 2025-11-12

Todo (short):
- [ ] Validate revocation_rate assumption against Aug–Oct 2025 telemetry (SRE)
- [ ] Add a compact one-line rule encoder that can be stored in routing metadata (e.g., JSON rule expression)
- [ ] Recompute numbers using 95th-token length (not mean) and include into rule thresholds

References and background links:
- Confluence: cost-modeling/optimize-tiered-fallback (CONFLUENCE-2342)
- GitHub: routing-sim (see data/spot-history-2025.csv)
- Slack threads: #optimize-routing (link pinned)

Notes to self:
- Keep the playbook short; we want the Console defaults to be useful without deep tuning.
- When in doubt, prefer simplicity: three tiers, three knobs, and a weekly re-run cost-reporting job that surfaces heavy tail customers to Sales/CS for potential Dedicated upsell.
